name: oauth2-upstream-authentication
description:
Authenticates outbound requests to an upstream backend using OAuth2. The gateway
exchanges credentials for a short-lived access token at a configured token endpoint
and injects it as an Authorization: Bearer header. The grant used is selected via
grantType: client_credentials (RFC 6749 4.4, the standard machine-to-machine grant)
or password (RFC 6749 4.3, Resource Owner Password Credentials, for legacy identity
providers). Client authentication uses clientAuthMethod - client_secret_basic
(default) or client_secret_post. Tokens are cached locally in-process for near-zero hot-path latency, and
additionally in Redis when Redis is configured and available, so every
gateway-runtime replica shares one token per API (not per resource/route -
the whole point being every resource an API exposes shares the same
credentials) instead of each replica fetching and caching its own. A
configurable tokenRequestTimeout bounds every token-endpoint call, and
defaultTokenTTL keeps caching working even if the identity provider omits
expires_in.
